sentences.text: Maybe I'll just turn down the lights a little.

alts.text: Let me dim the lights a bit.
Perhaps I will lower the lights slightly.

sentences.note: **turn down**은 불빛, 소리, 온도를 줄일 때 두루 씁니다. 앞에 **Maybe I'll just**를 붙이면 '그냥 이렇게 좀 해 볼까' 하는 가벼운 말투가 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: All right, we can work out that name later.

alts.text: Okay, let's figure out the name later.
Very well, we can decide on that name at a later time.

sentences.note: **work out**은 같이 이야기해서 정리하거나 결정한다는 뜻입니다. 지금 당장 정하지 말고 미뤄 두자고 할 때 **we can work out**을 많이 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 너희 이거 알고 있었으면서 우리한테 말 안 했구나.
sentences.text: You guys knew about this and you didn't tell us.

alts.text: Wait, you knew and didn't say anything?
So you were aware of this and did not inform us.

sentences.note: **knew about this**는 '이 일을 이미 알고 있었다'는 뜻입니다. 뒤에 **and you didn't tell us**를 붙이면 '알면서 말을 안 했다'는 서운함이 드러납니다. 깜짝 소식을 늦게 들었을 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아직 낮잠 잘 시간이긴 한데, 곧 깰 거야.
sentences.text: It's still nap time, but she'll be up soon.

alts.text: She's napping, but not for long.
She is still napping at the moment, but she will wake up shortly.

sentences.note: **nap time**은 아이가 정해진 시간에 낮잠 자는 때를 말합니다. **be up**은 '잠에서 깨어 있다'는 뜻이라, 아기 보러 온 손님에게 '곧 깰 거야'라고 할 때 딱 맞습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 있잖아, 걔 그냥 우리랑 얘기하느라 진이 다 빠졌던 걸지도 몰라.
sentences.text: You know, maybe she was just really spent from our talk.

alts.text: She was probably just wiped after that talk.
Perhaps she was simply exhausted from our conversation.

sentences.note: **spent**는 기운을 다 써서 녹초가 됐다는 뜻으로, tired보다 훨씬 지친 느낌입니다. 힘든 대화나 일을 하고 나서 **really spent**라고 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 너는 그냥 해야 할 일을 한 거야.
sentences.text: You just did what you had to do.

alts.text: Hey, you had no choice.
There was nothing else you could have done.

sentences.note: **did what you had to do** 는 힘든 결정을 내리고 마음 쓰는 사람을 달랠 때 씁니다. '어쩔 수 없었잖아, 네 잘못 아니야'라는 위로입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 의사가 그 말을 믿어 줄 줄은 몰랐어.
sentences.text: I didn't think the doctor was going to buy that.

alts.text: Never thought the doc would fall for it.
I did not expect the doctor to believe that.

sentences.note: **buy that** 은 '그 말을 믿다'라는 뜻으로, 핑계나 둘러댄 말이 먹혔을 때 씁니다. 비슷하게 **fall for it** 은 '거기 넘어가다'입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 나 잠깐 하나만 빨리 하고 올게.
sentences.text: I just have to do one thing really quickly.

alts.text: Gimme a sec, gotta do one thing.
Please give me a moment; there is one thing I need to take care of.

sentences.note: 나가기 전이나 통화를 끊기 전에 잠깐 기다려 달라고 할 때 **really quickly** 를 끝에 붙이면 '금방 끝난다'는 느낌이 납니다. **Gimme a sec** 도 같은 자리에서 많이 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그동안은 그냥 마음 편히 있어. 여기 다 괜찮아 보이니까.
sentences.text: And in the meantime, just relax because everything here looks great.

alts.text: Meanwhile, chill — it all looks good.
Until then, please do not worry, since everything appears to be fine.

sentences.note: **in the meantime** 는 '결과가 나올 때까지 그 사이에'라는 뜻입니다. 검사 결과나 연락을 기다리는 사람을 안심시킬 때 자주 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 미안한데, 얘는 왠지 이사벨라라는 이름이랑 안 어울려.
sentences.text: I'm sorry, she just doesn't feel like an Isabella.

alts.text: Sorry, she's not really an Isabella.
I apologize, but the name Isabella does not seem to suit her.

sentences.note: **doesn't feel like an Isabella** 처럼 이름 앞에 an 을 붙이면 '그런 이름이 어울리는 사람'이라는 뜻이 됩니다. 아기나 반려동물 이름을 지을 때 '이 이름은 아닌 것 같아'라고 하는 자리에 딱 맞습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends
